notes: This baseline validates the default qemu-nonx86-experimental-asm scenario result, not the compiler-ready promotion lane.
Default non-x86 QEMU platforms are linux/arm/v7 linux/arm64 linux/riscv64 unless SIMD_QEMU_PLATFORMS_NONX86 overrides them.
Default execution keeps SIMD_QEMU_ENABLE_BACKEND_ASM=0, so the scenario is expected to PASS without per-backend asm defines.
If SIMD_QEMU_ENABLE_BACKEND_ASM=1, default probe mode (SIMD_QEMU_BACKEND_ASM_PROBE_MODE=1) may retry a fallback path without per-backend asm defines and still keep the scenario PASS.
Compiler-ready promotion evidence for FAFAFA_SIMD_NEON_ASM_COMPILER_READY and FAFAFA_SIMD_RISCVV_ASM_COMPILER_READY lives in experimental_asm_compiler_ready_blockers.md.

RVV opcode-ready validation stays in riscvv-opcode-lane; keep SIMD_QEMU_EXPERIMENTAL_RISCV64_OPCODE_DEFINE unset in the default QEMU probe lane unless explicitly exercising patched opcode-ready toolchains.
An empty platforms map means no platform-specific failure signatures are currently expected; any FAIL row is treated as drift.
